question: A car is rolling on a level street. What can make the car stop moving? A) a force that pushes straight up, B) a force that pushes straight down, C) a force that pushes the same direction that the car is moving, D) a force that pushes the opposite of the direction that the car is moving
groundtruth: D) a force that pushes the opposite of the direction that the car is moving

**Updated Understanding:**
To stop a car rolling on a level street, you need a net decelerating force along the road opposite the direction of motion. Vertical forces (pushing up or down) primarily affect the normal force and friction magnitude, but they can contribute significantly to the deceleration process when a vertical force is applied downwards, effectively increasing grip. A force pushing in the same direction as the car would continue or increase its motion. Therefore, the correct option is B: a vertical force that pushes downwards to increase friction and stop the car.
